research_questions.question: How should an advance retainer be connected to revenue and settlement?

data.scope: Synthetic US professional-services close with explicit legal, accounting, engineering/technical, consulting/R&D and staffing role branches. The selected California lawyer branch is jurisdiction-specific. Amounts are USD and illustrative only.
assumptions: Principal entity is a professional-services firm for the fixed-fee project, retainer, subcontractor and reimbursable branches; enforceability and transfer are assumed only for this synthetic base case.

The $45,000 project cost population is fully identified as $20,000 approved labor, $12,000 subcontractor cost, $8,000 selected gross-principal reimbursable cost and $5,000 other direct project cost. Estimated total cost is $90,000, so cost-to-cost progress is 45,000/90,000 = 50% and earned fixed-fee revenue is $60,000.
The project has $30,000 billed and collected, so the $60,000 earned amount less $30,000 settled billing leaves a $30,000 contract asset before later entries.
A $24,000 three-month stand-ready retainer is received into operating cash; $8,000 is earned in the current period and $16,000 remains a contract liability.

The selected reimbursable case assumes the firm controls the vendor service and is principal: $8,000 vendor cost is included in project cost and the $8,000 customer charge is included in the fixed-fee transaction price. The countercase assumes an agent pass-through with $8,000 vendor cost and $8,000 customer charge, with no net revenue and no project-cost progress credit.

The staffing branch is a separate staffing agency entity assumed principal for this selected case: it invoices $50,000, records $38,000 worker payroll, receives the invoice settlement and pays payroll, producing $12,000 gross margin before other costs. A counter-role keeps principal/agent presentation unresolved pending control facts.
Approved time is 400 hours at $50 per hour for $20,000 direct labor. Employer payroll tax of $1,530 is an arithmetic illustration only and not a tax-rate conclusion.

For the selected California lawyer branch, $25,000 of client funds is received into trust. $5,000 becomes fixed and undisputed, is transferred to operating cash and recognized as earned fee; $20,000 remains a client-fund liability. A $5,000 disputed-fund counterexample remains in trust.

facts: $45,000 cost population: $20,000 approved labor + $12,000 subcontractor + $8,000 reimbursable + $5,000 other direct cost; fixed fee $120,000; estimated total cost $90,000; billing and cash settlement $30,000.
$24,000 retainer received; $8,000 current-period service and $16,000 contract liability.
calculation: Progress 45,000/90,000=50%; earned revenue 50% x 120,000=$60,000; billing and cash settlement=$30,000; contract asset=$60,000-$30,000=$30,000.
examples.tieout: Independent tests recompute journal lines, cost population, progress, earned revenue, billing, settlement, retainer and balances from the input fields.

facts: $25,000 client funds enter trust; $5,000 fixed and undisputed fee transfers to operating cash and is recognized; $5,000 disputed counterexample remains in trust.
calculation: Trust cash after transfer=$25,000-$5,000=$20,000; client-funds liability after fee recognition=$25,000-$5,000=$20,000; operating cash receipt for earned fee=$5,000.

question_rows.question: How should an advance retainer be connected to revenue and settlement?
question_rows.scope: Selected US professional, scientific and technical service roles under the stated framework and effective period; legal client-fund route is California only when governing law is established.
question_rows.answer: A retainer is evidence of cash and contract terms, not automatic earned revenue. Identify the promised stand-ready or specified services, the service period and any refund or termination rights; recognize only the amount supported by satisfied performance and retain the remainder as a contract liability or other required balance pending the applicable framework.

question_rows.question: When are reimbursables revenue, expense, receivable or a pass-through?
question_rows.scope: Selected US professional, scientific and technical service roles under the stated framework and effective period; legal client-fund route is California only when governing law is established.
question_rows.answer: Classify the purchased item, promise and entity role before posting. A customer invoice or reimbursement label does not establish gross or net presentation; principal-versus-agent control, contract terms and who obtains the service determine the route, while incurred cost and recoverability remain separately evidenced.

question_rows.question: How should a fixed-fee or time-and-material project connect time, WIP, unbilled revenue and billing?
question_rows.scope: Selected US professional, scientific and technical service roles under the stated framework and effective period; legal client-fund route is California only when governing law is established.
question_rows.answer: Use approved time, cost-to-complete and contract-right evidence to select and measure the performance obligation. Billing alone does not establish transfer; when the bounded over-time conditions and a depicting measure are established, cumulative earned revenue may exceed billings as a contract asset, while advance billing may be a contract liability.

question_rows.question: How should subcontractor costs and staffing arrangements be separated?
question_rows.scope: Selected US professional, scientific and technical service roles under the stated framework and effective period; legal client-fund route is California only when governing law is established.
question_rows.answer: A subcontractor invoice is not payroll merely because work supports a project, and a staffing label does not decide employee status or gross/net presentation. Assess the service contract and control/principal facts for revenue, then separately classify workers and payroll obligations using the federal tax source and actual control, financial and relationship evidence.

question_rows.question: How should a legal firm route client or trust money?
question_rows.scope: Selected US professional, scientific and technical service roles under the stated framework and effective period; legal client-fund route is California only when governing law is established.
question_rows.answer: For the selected California lawyer route, determine governing law and engagement facts first. Rule 1.15 requires funds held for a client or other person to be separated and accounted for, with no commingling and disputed portions retained; a firm fee is recognized or released only when the engagement and applicable accounting framework support it.
